source.title: HybridStitch: Pixel and Timestep Level Model Stitching for Diffusion Acceleration
source.authors: De-Sen Sun; Jason Hon; Jintao Zhang; Si-Hang Liu

record.tranche_reason: The study uses small–large prediction disagreement and confidence to route diffusion-model computation, but it does not test representation alignment.
record.gate_note: The study measures agreement between model predictions, not similarity between representations or distances induced on shared inputs. Those output-agreement results are recorded under fits_no_version; the efficiency and allocation results do not measure the claim.
record.test_reason: HybridStitch is an inference-efficiency method that routes token updates between a small and a large diffusion model. It measures output agreement (velocity discrepancy, token-match rate), not representation similarity. It never maps between the two models' representations: each model keeps its own KV buffers. It does not cite or rely on representation convergence, so T6 fits better than the reader's T4.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that token-level, feedback-driven allocation between small and large models, with model-specific KV caches, gives 1.63–1.68× image speedup and 1.15–1.58× dLLM throughput at comparable quality.
record.recipe_differences: The study routes model predictions during diffusion generation; it does not use a representation-alignment or representation-comparison method.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported small–large token agreement varies with small-model confidence; the text also reports that T2I velocity prediction differences decrease during denoising.

fits_no_version.finding: On MATH500, SDAR-1.7B tokens match SDAR-8B 99.5% of the time at confidence ≥0.99, falling to 36.5% below 0.5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For same-family diffusion LMs of different sizes, small–large output agreement rises with small-model confidence.

fits_no_version.finding: Velocity prediction differences between SD3 Medium and SD3.5 Large decrease along the denoising trajectory and vary across spatial tokens.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small–large diffusion-model output discrepancy varies with denoising step and token position.

record.problems: The study does not measure representations or induced distances, so its prediction-agreement results cannot establish representation convergence. The T2I discrepancy result is presented in a figure without numerical values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Efficiency, quality, and allocation results were left out because they do not measure representation alignment or prediction agreement. No representation-alignment results are reported.

untested.parts: All of it: no representation similarity across model scale or capability.
All of it: no image–caption representation alignment.
All of it: no comparison across seeds.
All of it. Despite the 'stitching' name, there is no mapping or stitching between representations; each model uses its own representation space.
All of it: no feature or circuit comparison.
All of it: no similarity metric is varied.
All of it: no alignment ceiling and no test of causes.

record.verdict_notes: The models compared are same-family pairs (SD3 Medium vs SD3.5 Large; SDAR-1.7B vs SDAR-8B), and only their outputs are compared. The efficiency, quality and ablation results are irrelevant to the claim. The reader's 'uses_without_test'/T4 is changed to T6 because the method does not rely on representation convergence.

versions.untested_parts: Representation alignment as models get larger or more capable; no representation or distance similarity is measured.
No paired image-caption representation alignment or relationship to vision/language model capability is measured.
No comparison across training seeds or measurement of shared features or subspaces.
No mapping, stitching, or other interchangeability test of representations.
No recurring interpretable features or circuits are identified or compared.
No representation-similarity measure, settings comparison, or out-of-distribution representation comparison is tested.
No test of representation-alignment plateaus or of shared data/objectives as an explanation for alignment.
